segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Settle into a position that feels kind enough for today. Imagine a tiny post office opening after sunset, staffed by patient fireflies.

[soft, slow, warm voice] Begin with a message addressed to you. May I be safe... may I be cared for... may I have moments of ease. Let the words glow without demanding that you believe them perfectly.
[soft, slow, warm voice] A firefly lifts the message gently and carries it around the quiet rooms of your body. Perhaps warmth arrives. Perhaps awkwardness does. Both can receive mail here.

[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft paper rustling] Now picture someone easy to wish well. Place their name on another small envelope. May you be safe... may you be cared for... may you have moments of ease.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [faint wind rustling leaves] Watch that light travel across gardens, rooftops, and sleeping streets. You do not need to know how the message lands.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Bring to mind a familiar stranger... someone seen on a bus, in a shop, or through a neighbouring window. Their life contains rooms you have never entered.
[soft, slow, warm voice] May you be safe... may you be cared for... may you have moments of ease. Another firefly rises into the common dark.

[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] Include someone difficult only if that feels workable. You can offer a modest wish without approving their actions: may wisdom and kindness become more possible.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the post office grow busy now. Thousands of small lights carry wishes toward animals, strangers, friends, and people awake beneath unfamiliar skies.
[soft, slow, warm voice] May we be safe... may we be cared for... may we have moments of ease. Let the sentence be a direction of the heart, not a promise about the world.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Release the words and feel the body breathing. The fireflies can continue their work without your supervision.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Return to the room. Open your eyes when ready, carrying one small undelivered kindness into the rest of your day.
